prompt: A command names no cluster. Where does kubectl send it?

choices.text: To the first cluster in the file
choices.why: Order in the file decides nothing.

choices.text: To every cluster in the file
choices.why: kubectl talks to one API server per command.
Only because kind set the pointer then.

prompt: What is the safest way for a deploy pipeline to choose its cluster?
hint: It should not depend on what ran before it.

choices.text: Run `kubectl config use-context` at the start
choices.why: That moves a pointer others share.

choices.text: Its own kubeconfig with one context
Trust whatever the agent's context is
choices.why: That is the incident in this lesson.

choices.text: Name the cluster in the Deployment
choices.why: A manifest has no cluster field.

prompt: Which three things does a context name?
hint: `kubectl config get-contexts` has a column for each.

choices.text: A node, a pod and a container
A region, a zone and a provider
An image, a tag and a registry
A cluster, a user and a namespace

prompt: Two clusters were made from the same configuration and both have a pod at `10.244.1.3`. What does that rule out?

choices.text: Running the same image in both
choices.why: Images do not care about addresses.

choices.text: Routing pod to pod between them

choices.why: The file has done that all lesson.
Each can have its own load balancer.

prompt: You are cluster-admin in staging. What does that give you in production?
hint: Each cluster has its own RBAC.

choices.why: Roles live in each cluster's etcd.

prompt: Why might a team that runs customers' code get a cluster of its own rather than a namespace?

choices.text: A cluster is cheaper than a namespace
choices.why: It is the more expensive option.
Right, and one etcd and one upgrade.

prompt: Which tool is the common way today to keep the same objects in many clusters?

choices.text: `kubectl apply` in a loop by hand
choices.why: It works once and drifts after.

prompt: What decides whether two regions can both serve writes at once?
hint: The stateless pods are the easy part.

choices.text: The number of nodes in each

choices.why: Kubernetes does not hold the data.
It sends traffic; it does not merge writes.
